title: Roll Forward and Undo Order Processor
description:
**SITUATION:**

Engineering ships Order Processor `v1.2` with a rolling update, then QA finds a bad template. You must **roll forward** with controlled surge settings, then **undo** to the previous revision — the everyday Deployment safety net (different from canary/blue-green cutovers).

This lab practices Deployment **rolling update + rollback** for Order Processor. Different from canary/blue-green: one Deployment, revision history, undo when QA says no.
**YOUR TASK:**

1. **Update** the Deployment to image `v1.2` with a RollingUpdate strategy (`maxSurge` / `maxUnavailable` as specified).
2. Wait until the rollout is complete.
3. **Roll back** to the previous revision.
4. Verify Pods are Ready on the rolled-back image.

**SPEC:**

- Deployment name: `order-processor-deploy`
- Strategy type: `RollingUpdate`
  - `maxSurge: 1`
  - `maxUnavailable: 0`
- First change image to: `rithvikreddyalkanti/order-processor:v1.2`
- Then run rollback (e.g. `kubectl rollout undo deployment/order-processor-deploy`)
- Final image on Pods: `rithvikreddyalkanti/order-processor:v1.1` (previous revision)
- Ready: **3/3** after rollback

**CONSTRAINTS:**

- Record the updated Deployment (pre-undo or post-strategy) in `order-processor-rollout-l40.yaml`; rollback may be imperative.
- Do **not** delete the Deployment to “fix” the version.
- Work only in your lab namespace (not `default`).

hints: Your namespace is in the lab chrome and in $LEARNER_NS — kubectl already defaults there.

problemStatement.solution:
# Solution — Roll Forward and Undo Order Processor

Stay in your lab namespace. Set RollingUpdate surge settings, roll Order Processor to `v1.2`, then **undo** to the previous revision (`v1.1`).

Docs: [Deployments — rolling update](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/controllers/deployment/#rolling-update-deployment) · [rollout undo](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/kubectl/generated/kubectl_rollout/kubectl_rollout_undo/)

## Solution YAML

Save as `order-processor-rollout-l40.yaml` (forward change before undo):

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: order-processor-deploy
spec:
  replicas: 3
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxSurge: 1
      maxUnavailable: 0
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: order-processor
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: order-processor
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: order-processor
          image: rithvikreddyalkanti/order-processor:v1.2
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8000
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: "100m"
              memory: "128Mi"
```

## Declarative

```bash
kubectl apply -f order-processor-rollout-l40.yaml
kubectl rollout status deploy/order-processor-deploy
kubectl set image deploy/order-processor-deploy order-processor=rithvikreddyalkanti/order-processor:v1.2  # if already applied via YAML
kubectl rollout undo deploy/order-processor-deploy
kubectl rollout status deploy/order-processor-deploy
kubectl get deploy order-processor-deploy -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image}{"\n"}'
```

Final image must be `rithvikreddyalkanti/order-processor:v1.1` with **3/3** Ready. Do not delete the Deployment to “fix” the version.
